text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Huge bank loans amounting to 9.782 billion rupees were written off by 1,418 companies and individuals in the last 11 years.
- The army will be deployed in every constituency to ensure security during the February 3 general elections, Defence Minister Shahid Hamid said.
- Following the death of four more people, the death toll of Wednesday's gas disaster in Lahore rose to 21, while about 100 are still under treatment in various hospitals.
- The caretaker government has again raised the prices of petroleum products.
- Defence Minister Shahid Hamid has said the Council for Defence and National Security has been constituted to formalise the role of the president in the affairs of state.
- Pakistani missions in Athens and Rome will help the surviving Pakistanis of a ship which sank off the coast of Sicily.

- The investment climate in Pakistan's most populous Punjab province seems to have been severely hit by political uncertainty as new projects worth 17 billion rupees, all in the private sector, have made no headway for the last three months.
- Federal Commerce Minister Zubair Khan has said Pakistan is pursuing a liberalised trade regime with lower tariffs which would be reduced to 35 percent in the next three years.

- The caretaker government is preparing over eight cases of corruption, favouritism and irregularities in the award of contracts of gold, zinc, salt, coal and other precious metals against the deposed government of Benazir Bhutto.
- Problems involving British companies operating in Pakistan will come under discussion for the removal of irritants during British Prime Minister John Major's visit to Pakistan.
- Prime Minister Meraj Khalid has ordered urgent financial aid for the victims of the leakage of poisonous gas in Lahore.
- The Defence Minister of Pakistan's caretaker government has said Islamabad would not slash its defence budget despite its economic woes as long as it faced a security threat.
